title: The Gary 'Demon House': What Police and Caseworkers Reported

sources.what: moved in Nov. 2011; flies swarming the porch in December; footsteps on the basement stairs; Capt. Charles Austin first thought them 'liars', later 'a believer'; DCS caseworker's report of the boy moving backward up a wall; psychologists' explanations; exorcisms by Rev. Michael Maginot with Bishop Melczek's approval, 2012; DCS custody 2012, returned Nov. 2012; house demolished early 2016; Austin: 'Why go where evil possibly is there?'
sources.who: The Indianapolis Star (Marisa Kwiatkowski, Jan. 25, 2014, and follow-ups), as carried by Gannett papers and WKYC

sources.what: 'phantom footsteps'; the police captain became 'a believer'; Zak Bagans bought the house for $35,000
from the records: the boy 'walked up the wall'; DCS removed the children; Rev. Maginot interview
bishop allowed the exorcism; house demolished early 2016
Austin: 'Why go where evil possibly is there?'; exorcisms
skeptical review: the grandmother held the boy's hand; 'no demons possessed anyone'

beats.text: The family said black flies swarmed their porch in the dead of winter. That's how it started, in a house in Gary.
beats.label: GARY, INDIANA

beats.text: In 2011, a mother and her three children moved in. Soon, they said, they heard footsteps on the basement stairs, late at night.
beats.label: WHAT THE FAMILY SAID

beats.text: A Gary police captain first suspected they'd made it up. After visiting the house, he said: I am a believer.
beats.label: THE POLICE CAPTAIN
beats.credit: The Indianapolis Star; ABC News; WKYC

beats.text: A state caseworker's report described a boy moving backward up a wall. Doctors and psychologists offered other explanations.
beats.label: THE CASEWORKER'S REPORT
beats.credit: The Indianapolis Star (DCS records); KTRK ABC13; Skeptical Inquirer

beats.text: In 2012, with his bishop's approval, a Catholic priest performed exorcisms on the mother, at his church.
beats.label: THE EXORCISMS
beats.credit: The Indianapolis Star; EWTN/CNA; National Catholic Register

beats.text: No one ever proved anything supernatural. In 2016, the house was torn down.
beats.label: TORN DOWN
beats.credit: The Indianapolis Star; EWTN/CNA; Skeptical Inquirer

beats.text: In 2014, the captain put it this way: Why go where evil possibly is there?
beats.label: THE CAPTAIN
beats.credit: The Indianapolis Star; National Catholic Register

beats.text: Comment your town for the next La Porte After Dark.

factcheck.result: Lines 2, 4, 6 supported. Flies attributed to the family; 'lying' became 'suspected they'd made it up' and 'went inside' became 'visiting'; the exorcisms were on the mother at the priest's church, not in the house; the 'evil' quote dated 2014 (before the demolition).
